matchedLines.text: Fixed You should know writing its notes in English regardless of the `language` setting
Improved "You should know" notes to say "we", "the main agent" or "you" depending on who was responsible for a decision

Added You should know, a built-in mod where a side agent watches your back and flags things you or Claude might miss. Turn it on with `/plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin` (for first-party sessions with telemetry on)

items.upstreamQuote: Added You should know, a built-in mod where a side agent watches your back and flags things you or Claude might miss. Turn it on with /plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin (for first-party sessions with telemetry on)
items.claim: A built-in side agent reviews completed work and flags important things the human or the agent most likely missed.
items.parityNotes: Implemented as an out-of-tree DeepSeek Harness plugin with a separately configured reviewer model. The user-visible capability matches; the platform, the enable path, and the human-only isolation differ by design and were verified on the shipped v0.4.3 code.

items.upstreamQuote: for first-party sessions with telemetry on
items.claim: The built-in mod is gated to first-party sessions that have telemetry enabled.
items.parityNotes: This plugin has no telemetry and no first-party session concept.
items.rejectionReason: Platform-specific upstream gating. Adopting it would require adding telemetry and a first-party session notion, which would weaken the documented privacy posture and is not part of this plugin's model.

items.upstreamQuote: Improved "You should know" notes to say "we", "the main agent" or "you" depending on who was responsible for a decision
items.claim: A note picks its voice from who was responsible for the decision: we, the main agent, or you.
items.parityNotes: Instruction-level adaptation, not proven behavioral equivalence. The upstream changelog asks for notes that name who was responsible; this plugin carries one explicit responsibility-attribution rule in the trusted base reviewer policy ("we" when the human and the agent decided together, "the main agent" when the action or choice is the agent's, "you" when the decision or the consequence is the human's or when the note addresses the human directly) plus a neutral statement of fact when the excerpt does not show who was responsible, and it never invents blame. What is verified: the composed system prompt contains that rule, keeps the base policy first, and does not gain a fabricated owner from the excerpt; see test/core.test.js and test/review-profile.test.js. What is NOT verified: the reviewer model's live output. The model is nondeterministic and no live-model test exercises it, so an actual note naming the responsible party is unproven. Status is adapted rather than equivalent for that reason.

acceptance.summary: The reviewer instruction selects the note voice by responsibility, as verified by prompt composition.
acceptance.testableAs: A prompt-composition test asserts that the composed reviewer system prompt carries the responsibility-attribution rule and its three voices, and that a Custom reviewer prompt cannot replace the base rule. Completed by the task ysk-note-voice-attribution-20261014; this acceptance covers instruction composition only, not live model behavior.

items.upstreamQuote: Fixed You should know writing its notes in English regardless of the language setting
items.claim: Notes follow the configured language setting instead of always being written in English.
items.parityNotes: lib/language.js resolves the output language with priority: explicit host user-language setting, then the latest genuine human message, then English. Covered by test/language.test.js and present before this baseline.

outagePolicy.rule: If any primary source is unreachable, moved, truncated, or otherwise unverifiable, the affected item is recorded as unknown for that cycle; it is never recorded as no change. The previous verified baseline stays in place, and the outage plus the attempted URLs are recorded in the next review update.
outagePolicy.appliesTo: every verification step, including the source list itself

lastOutage.what: The GitHub-hosted endpoints (raw.githubusercontent.com, api.github.com) and the docs host resolved to non-public addresses in this environment, so this cycle re-read the served official changelog page instead.

openUnknowns.question: How the upstream side agent selects, gates, deduplicates, and formats its notes.
openUnknowns.whyUnknown: The official release note and changelog do not describe the algorithm, and this repository does not reverse engineer undisclosed internals.
openUnknowns.reassessWhen: An official Anthropic source discloses the behavior.

openUnknowns.question: How the upstream mod handles session data under its telemetry gate.
openUnknowns.whyUnknown: The official text does not describe data handling. Assuming it matches this plugin's privacy model would be speculation.
openUnknowns.reassessWhen: An official Anthropic privacy or data-flow statement covers the mod.
